items.title: Post-Train NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge for On-Device Robot Control
items.summary: NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge is a 4B omnimodel with a 2B NVIDIA Nemotron-based reasoner that has been pretrained on the same physical-world data as NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Nano and NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Super. It starts with the same grounding in how objects move and interact and is small enough to run on-device on NVIDIA Jetson Thor. The model can be used to predict robot actions and has been evaluated in closed-loop simulation, reaching 22.9% success across 120 language-conditioned manipulation tasks.
items.audio_script: From NVIDIA Developer Blog, "Post-Train NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge for On-Device Robot Control," it appears that NVIDIA has successfully developed a new version of its Cosmos 3 model, specifically designed for on-device robot control. The Cosmos 3 Edge is a 4B omnimodel that features a 2B NVIDIA Nemotron-based reasoner, pre-trained on the same physical-world data as its smaller counterparts, the Cosmos 3 Nano and Cosmos 3 Super. This approach enables the model to share a common grounding in understanding how objects move and interact, allowing it to be smaller and more power-efficient. The Cosmos 3 Edge has been evaluated in closed-loop simulation, achieving a 22.9% success rate across 120 language-conditioned manipulation tasks.

items.title: Global Humanoid Shipments Surpass 22,000 in H1 2026 as AGIBOT Leads and Form-Factor Debates Intensify
items.summary: Global humanoid robot shipments exceeded 22,000 units in the first half of 2026, with AGIBOT leading the market with 9,700 shipments (43.1% market share), followed by Unitree with 7,000 units (31.1%). The top five vendors controlled over 86% of the market, with entertainment, performance, and data-collection research accounting for over 60% of deliveries.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, "Global Humanoid Shipments Surpass 22,000 in H1 2026 as AGIBOT Leads and Form-Factor Debates Intensify." Global humanoid robot shipments have exceeded 22,000 units in the first half of 2026, with AGIBOT leading the market with 9,700 shipments, accounting for 43.1% of the total. AGIBOT's dominance is followed by Unitree, which delivered 7,000 units, making up 31.1% of the market. The top five vendors, including AGIBOT and Unitree, collectively controlled over 86% of the market share. The market is driven by entertainment, performance, and data-collection research, with these segments accounting for over 60% of the deliveries. This significant milestone indicates a growing trend in humanoid robot adoption, with key form-factor debates expected to intensify in the coming months.

items.title: Waymo is bringing Gemini into its custom Ojai vehicles.
items.summary: Waymo is integrating Gemini into its custom Ojai vehicles to provide a more personalized ride experience. Gemini is an in-car AI assistant that can be controlled using voice commands, allowing riders to control the cabin, learn about their surroundings, and access information on nearby attractions. Gemini operates independently of the Waymo Driver and is only active when engaged by the rider.
items.audio_script: From Google / Google AI (Keyword Blog), "Waymo is bringing Gemini into its custom Ojai vehicles." This story reports that Waymo is integrating Gemini, an in-car AI assistant, into its bespoke Ojai vehicles, aiming to enhance the passenger experience. Gemini, which can be controlled using voice commands, will enable riders to adjust cabin settings, gather information on nearby attractions, and access various features independently of the Waymo Driver. According to the integration, Gemini will operate in a separate instance, allowing it to process voice commands and respond accordingly. This integration is part of Waymo's ongoing effort to improve its autonomous ride-hailing services.

items.title: MIT engineers design a better controller for operating construction diggers
items.summary: MIT engineers have designed a new, more intuitive controller for operating construction diggers, which uses a miniature excavator's arm and bucket to mimic the machine's movements, eliminating the need for mental mapping and potentially shortening the training process for operators. The new interface, named the "World-Space Interface," pairs the mechanical arm with a virtual simulation of an excavator, allowing operators to physically operate the machine in a virtual environment. The team reports that novices using the WSI were just as good as experts from the start, compared to the traditional joystick-based simulator, which required novices to learn complex mental maps.
items.audio_script: From MIT News - Robotics, "MIT engineers design a better controller for operating construction diggers," MIT engineers have designed a new, more intuitive controller for operating construction diggers, which utilizes a miniature excavator's arm and bucket to mimic the machine's movements, effectively eliminating the need for mental mapping. The new interface, named the "World-Space Interface," pairs the mechanical arm with a virtual simulation of an excavator, allowing operators to physically operate the machine in a virtual environment. This method was achieved through the integration of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and human-centered design principles. Initial results show that novices using the WSI were equally proficient as experts from the start, contrasting with traditional joystick-based simulators that required novices to learn complex mental maps.

items.title: X Square Robot showcases full embodied AI portfolio at WRC 2026
items.summary: X Square Robot is showcasing its full portfolio of embodied AI technologies at the World Robot Conference 2026 in Beijing, presenting applications in logistics automation, dexterous manipulation, household robotics, and AI training-data collection. The company's WALL-B embodied AI foundation model, robotic hardware, manipulation technologies, and data infrastructure are on display at booth C107. X Square Robot's demonstrations include a logistics system that processed 1,816 parcels with an accuracy of over 98 percent and a flower-arranging demo that tests the robot's ability to understand natural-language instructions and perform complex manipulation tasks.

items.title: From Marathons to the Factory Floor: Beijing’s World Humanoid Robot Games Pivot to Real-World Utility
items.summary: The second World Humanoid Robot Games (WHRG) kicks off on August 22 in Beijing, with 2,056 robots from 666 teams across 16 countries participating. The event has shifted focus toward commercial utility, introducing 21 scenario-based events that test robots in simulated factory, hotel, and retail environments. Autonomy rules have been tightened, with task time limits slashed and remote-controlled operations facing severe scoring penalties. The event aims to test whether humanoid robots can perform reliable, autonomous work to generate economic value.
items.audio_script:
From Humanoids Daily, "From Marathons to the Factory Floor: Beijing’s World Humanoid Robot Games Pivot to Real-World Utility". The second World Humanoid Robot Games (WHRG) is set to kick off on August 22 in Beijing, with 2,056 robots from 666 teams across 16 countries participating in a shift towards commercial utility, introducing 21 scenario-based events that test robots in simulated factory, hotel, and retail environments.

The event has undergone significant changes, with task time limits slashed and remote-controlled operations facing severe scoring penalties. This is done to test whether humanoid robots can perform reliable, autonomous work to generate economic value. The tournament organizers have also strengthened autonomy rules, aiming to assess robots' ability to adapt to changing situations and tasks. The new events and rules will push robots to navigate complex scenarios, such as assembling products, delivering packages, and interacting with customers. By evaluating robots' performance in these simulated environments, the event aims to inform real-world applications and deployments.

The WHRG 2023 will pave the way for the adoption of humanoid robots in various industries, from manufacturing to service sectors. Its focus on commercial utility and real-world scenarios will help accelerate the development of more practical and efficient robots. The event's findings and insights will provide valuable insights for researchers, manufacturers, and businesses looking to integrate humanoid robots into their operations.

items.title: How Automated T-Shirt Printing Machines Are Transforming Textile Production
items.summary: Automated T-shirt printing machines are revolutionizing the textile industry by supporting businesses in printing more shirts in less time, making the work easier and minimizing errors. These machines can print various designs, including company logos, pictures, names, numbers, and colorful designs, producing clear, vibrant, and neat prints. They offer several benefits, including faster printing, better print quality, less manual work, fewer mistakes, and lower production costs.
items.audio_script:
From Robotics & Automation News, "How Automated T-Shirt Printing Machines Are Transforming Textile Production". This story highlights how automated T-shirt printing machines are increasing the speed and efficiency of textile production, allowing businesses to print more shirts in less time.

Automated T-shirt printing machines are being widely adopted by textile companies, with several manufacturers reporting significant improvements in print quality and reduced production costs. These machines use advanced technology to quickly print various designs onto shirts, including company logos, pictures, names, numbers, and colorful designs, producing clear, vibrant, and neat prints. The process involves loading the shirts and design onto the machine, which then uses inkjet or screen printing technology to apply the desired design. By automating this process, companies are able to reduce manual work, minimize errors, and lower their production costs. As a result, textile production is becoming faster, more efficient, and more cost-effective.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: ROS 2 Inspector — Static Architecture Analysis and Visualization for ROS 2 Workspaces
items.summary: ROS 2 Inspector is an open-source project aimed at automating the architectural pass for ROS 2 workspaces. It uses static analysis to provide a compact summary of the discovered ROS 2 packages and their health signals. The tool generates interactive visualizations and can export data in table, JSON, or YAML formats. ROS 2 Inspector is not intended to replace runtime tools, as dynamic names and behavior can only be fully understood with runtime evidence.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: ROS 2 Inspector — Static Architecture Analysis and Visualization for ROS 2 Workspaces," ROS 2 Inspector is a tool designed to automate the architectural pass for ROS 2 workspaces, utilizing static analysis to provide a compact summary of discovered ROS 2 packages and their health signals. The tool generates interactive visualizations, offering data export in table, JSON, or YAML formats. ROS 2 Inspector was developed to assist developers in comprehensively understanding the architecture of ROS 2 workspaces, providing a foundation for more efficient and effective development. By leveraging static analysis, ROS 2 Inspector delivers a detailed analysis of ROS 2 packages, enabling users to identify and address potential issues before runtime. This marks a significant advancement in static analysis capabilities for ROS 2 workspaces.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: VirtuLayer - A GUI for Nav2 Virtual Layer Plugin
items.summary: VirtuLayer is a web-based GUI developed to simplify the configuration and usage of the Nav2 Virtual Layer Plugin. It provides a visual interface for creating virtual geometries on a map and generating the required configuration. The plugin can be used to add virtual geometries to the Nav2 costmap, allowing for a simple visual workflow for creating and experimenting with virtual layers.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: VirtuLayer - A GUI for Nav2 Virtual Layer Plugin." A web-based GUI called VirtuLayer has been developed to simplify the configuration and usage of the Nav2 Virtual Layer Plugin, allowing users to create virtual geometries on a map and generate the required configuration. The plugin, which can be used to add virtual geometries to the Nav2 costmap, enables a simple visual workflow for creating and experimenting with virtual layers. By providing a visual interface, VirtuLayer simplifies the process of configuring and using the Nav2 Virtual Layer Plugin, making it more accessible to users. The development of VirtuLayer marks a significant improvement in the usability of the Nav2 Virtual Layer Plugin.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: A runtime that sits between an LLM and physical actuation - Does this fit your use case?
items.summary: A researcher has developed a runtime called xZane that sits between an LLM and physical actuation, validating commands against device capabilities before execution, and running independently of the model. The approach has been tested on various devices, including a mobile robot, LG webOS TV, and robot vacuum, with similar results across different models and environments. The xZane runtime differs from related work, such as ROSClaw and URML, by integrating a device's existing safety function and avoiding the safety-critical path of the model. The researcher is seeking feedback from others to determine if the approach fits their use cases.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: A runtime that sits between an LLM and physical actuation - Does this fit your use case?" This story reports on the development of a runtime called xZane, a runtime that validates commands against device capabilities before execution, and runs independently of the LLM. The researcher has tested the xZane runtime on various devices, including a mobile robot, LG webOS TV, and robot vacuum, with similar results across different models and environments. The xZane runtime differs from related work, such as ROSClaw and URML, by integrating a device's existing safety function and avoiding the safety-critical path of the model. The researcher is now seeking feedback from others to determine if the approach fits their use cases, allowing the xZane runtime to be adapted for a broader range of applications.

items.title: Scheduling and Routing with Degradation-Triggered Job Arrivals: An Application to Forest Firefighting with an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Fleet
items.summary: Authors developed a mixed-integer programming model to maximize value retention in wildfire-threatened regions through scheduling and routing of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) fleets. The model considers degradation-triggered job arrivals, where new jobs appear when the demand of the existing job surpasses a threshold. The overall objective is to maximize the total remaining reward, aligning with the proverb "a stitch in time saves nine." The model is scalable, and its performance is evaluated through computational experiments and a case study.

items.title: Trust as a Field: A Macroscopic Representation for Vehicular Networks
items.summary: Researchers Md Mahmudul Islam and Shaurya Agarwal propose a trust-field framework that aggregates microscopic vehicle-level trust into a continuous representation over space and time for vehicular networks. The framework is formally defined on road segments and enables analysis of trust evolution across road segments through simulation-based experiments. A field-informed deep learning method that treats trust as a latent quantity carried by vehicles and enforces measurement consistency through aggregation yields improved reconstruction error.

items.title: Revisiting the "Push-T" Robot Manipulation Task with Agentic Robotics
items.summary: A robot is prompted to create an algorithmic solution to the "Push-T" task without human demonstrations, using an LLM coding agent. The agent learns push mechanics using a 2D gym simulation and achieves a 100% success rate with 46% fewer steps than a baseline. The agent also solves extensions of the task using a self-generated curriculum and visual feedback.

items.title: GigaBrain-WBC-0.5: A Behavior World Model for Robust Whole-Body Control with Environment Interaction
items.summary: GigaBrain-WBC-0.5 is a Behavior World Model for humanoid whole-body control, enabling robust interaction with environment and staying robust to implausible commands, falls, and disturbances. It achieves the highest success rate across all four regimes among three large-scale tracker baselines. The model achieves 81.3% success rate on terrain interaction, 83.1% under implausible commands, and 99.3% fall recovery. Hardware trials show robust interaction under missing supports and disturbances.

items.title: GAPL: Grounded Action-effect Policy Learning for LLM-Based Trajectory Planning
items.summary: GAPL (Grounded Action-effect Policy Learning) is a unified framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) with simulation-based effect grounding and policy optimization. The framework consists of three modules: an LLM-based Effect Evaluator, a Simulation-based Effect Grounder, and an Effect-Aware Decision Maker. Experiments on four Highway-env scenarios demonstrate that GAPL outperforms baselines, achieving average reductions of 0.76, 0.86, 2.00 in collision rate, average displacement error, and final displacement error, and an average reward gain of 1.44.

items.title: VERAGMIL: Virtual Environment for Scooping Granular Foods with Imitation Learning Models
items.summary: VERAGMIL, a framework combining a high-fidelity simulator and a virtual reality interface, provides a realistic environment for training robot-assisted feeding systems to handle granular materials. The framework is evaluated with three imitation learning models, achieving the best overall performance, particularly in reducing spillage, and approaching human performance. The code for VERAGMIL is publicly available.

items.title: A Task-Agnostic Control Strategy for Dynamic Assistance with Pneumatically Actuated Soft Exosuits
items.summary: A task-agnostic control strategy for dynamic assistance with pneumatically actuated soft exosuits was developed, relying only on kinematic sensing. The strategy uses a Hammerstein dynamic model to capture static and dynamic behavior of the human-robot system, and approximates an inverse to integrate into the control loop. The controller reduced interaction torque by up to 73% and activation of key muscles by up to 47% when evaluated on a test rig. The control strategy provides task-agnostic, dynamic assistance without the need for physiological or force sensors to interpret user intention.

items.title: The Embodiment Gap in Robot Foundation Models
items.summary: Robot foundation models, including vision-language-action policies, often focus on scaling up data, models, and benchmarks, but practical deployment on a target robot requires additional work. This work is categorized into the "embodiment gap," which includes shared structures and adaptation needed for execution on a new robot. Recent work addresses sharing semantics and perception, robot data and interfaces, and learning correspondence across embodiments. A reporting framework for adaptation work highlights the need to investigate what should be checked when comparing cross-embodiment learning.
